$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

# npm and electron-builder expect a SemVer version.
$semverPattern = '^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(?:-((?:0|[1-9][0-9]*|[0-9A-Za-z-]*[A-Za-z-][0-9A-Za-z-]*)(?:\.(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*|[0-9A-Za-z-]*[A-Za-z-][0-9A-Za-z-]*))*))?(?:\+[0-9A-Za-z-]+(?:\.[0-9A-Za-z-]+)*)?$'
if ($Version -cnotmatch $semverPattern) {
    throw "Invalid version '$Version'. Expected a SemVer version such as 1.2.3 or 1.2.3-beta.1."
}

$repositoryRoot = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
$encoding = New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false, $true)
$versionLinePattern = '^(?<prefix>  "version"[ \t]*:[ \t]*")(?<version>[^"]+)(?<suffix>"[ \t]*,?[ \t\r]*)$'
$updates = @(
    foreach ($project in @('app', 'desktop')) {
        $manifestPath = Join-Path $repositoryRoot "$project/package.json"
        $original = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllText($manifestPath, $encoding)
        $manifest = $original | ConvertFrom-Json
        if ($null -eq $manifest.version -or $manifest.version -isnot [string]) {
            throw "Missing version in $manifestPath"
        }

        $matches = [regex]::Matches($original, $versionLinePattern, [System.Text.RegularExpressions.RegexOptions]::Multiline)
        if ($matches.Count -ne 1 -or $matches[0].Groups['version'].Value -cne $manifest.version) {
            throw "Expected exactly one top-level version line in $manifestPath"
        }

        $match = $matches[0]
        $replacement = $match.Groups['prefix'].Value + $Version + $match.Groups['suffix'].Value
        $updated = $original.Substring(0, $match.Index) + $replacement + $original.Substring($match.Index + $match.Length)
        @{ Path = $manifestPath; Original = $original; Updated = $updated }
    }
)

$written = @()
try {
    foreach ($update in $updates) {
        if ($update.Original -ceq $update.Updated) { continue }
        $written += $update
        [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($update.Path, $update.Updated, $encoding)
    }
} catch {
    foreach ($update in $written) {
        [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($update.Path, $update.Original, $encoding)
    }
    throw
}

Write-Output "Updated app and desktop package.json to $Version"

const { spawn } = require('node:child_process');
const path = require('node:path');

const repositoryRoot = path.resolve(__dirname, '..', '..');

function runNpm(args, spawnImplementation = spawn) {
    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
        const child = spawnImplementation('npm', args, {
            cwd: repositoryRoot,
            env: process.env,
            shell: process.platform === 'win32',
            stdio: 'inherit',
        });

        child.once('error', reject);
        child.once('exit', (code, signal) => {
            if (signal) {
                reject(new Error(`npm ${args.join(' ')} stopped by signal ${signal}`));
                return;
            }
            if (code !== 0) {
                reject(new Error(`npm ${args.join(' ')} failed with exit code ${code}`));
                return;
            }

            resolve();
        });
    });
}

async function buildWindows(runNpmImplementation = runNpm) {
    await runNpmImplementation(['run', 'build', '--prefix', 'app']);
    await runNpmImplementation(['run', 'package:windows', '--prefix', 'desktop']);
}

if (require.main === module) {
    buildWindows().catch((error) => {
        console.error(error.message);
        process.exitCode = 1;
    });
}

module.exports = { buildWindows, runNpm };

tried to start an action on a card, got this error:

> 1 failed action

* (main): Card has no frontmatter: design/feature descriptions/F\_288\_clear\_dashboard\_values.md



it makes little sense. the card was simply available in the UI. We did remove a flush when selecting an agent, but the flush should happen when starting the action, most likely this got removed as well. check it

## Current state

- Reproduction clarified: `+` (custom prompt) starts a new agent conversation on a saved card. Failure repeats after saving.
- `runElectronAction()` in `app/src/services/actions/electron_action_runner.ts` already awaits `projectPersistenceService.flushPendingChanges()` when saves are pending, before starting the action. Flush means transferring editor buffers into service state, persisting queued changes, and awaiting storage writes. Selecting an action only flushes action-definition drafts through `action_popup_defaults.ts`.
- Conversation reservation in `desktop/src/actions/action/action_runner_service.js` allocates conversation identity; it does not read or write the card. During startup, `agent_conversation_persistence.js` writes initial activity, then `card_activity_reference.js` appends its path to the card's `agents` field before the agent process starts.
- Verified defect: `splitFrontmatter()` chooses CRLF if any CRLF occurs anywhere in the document. An LF header with a CRLF body therefore throws `Card has no frontmatter`, although renderer parsing through `shared/markdown_header_fields.mjs` accepts that header. LF means `\n`; CRLF means `\r\n`. Frontmatter means the opening metadata block enclosed by `---` lines.

I added the three sections to `design/feature_descriptions/F_419_write_release_script.md` and set `status: ready for implementation`. Nothing is staged or committed.

**Your four decisions, now in the doc:**
- **Release notes folder:** use the version with dots, e.g. `design/releases/0.8.3`. This replaces the spec's "replace `.` with `_`" rule.
- **Tag format:** `v<version>`, e.g. `v0.8.3`. Old tags like `V_0_7_1` stay as they are.
- **GitHub access:** through the `gh` CLI. It is not installed on this machine yet, so the doc lists installing it and running `gh auth login` as a prerequisite.
- **Script:** PowerShell, at `scripts/publish_release.ps1`, with a test file `scripts/publish_release.test.ps1`. This follows the pattern of `scripts/update_version.ps1`.

**Things I chose myself (change any you don't like):**
- **Frontmatter removed from notes:** `release_notes.md` starts with an md2 metadata block (`---` lines holding `internalId`). The script removes it so it doesn't appear in the GitHub release text.
- **Tag points at the checked-out commit:** the tag goes on whatever commit is checked out when the script runs.
- **Draft first, then publish:** the release is created as a draft with the installer attached, and published only after the upload succeeds. This avoids a public release with a missing installer.
- **Checks before any GitHub change:** the script stops before touching GitHub if the notes file, the installer, or `gh` is missing, or if the tag already exists.
- **No automatic rollback:** if something fails after the tag is pushed, the script leaves GitHub as is and prints the commands to clean up by hand.
- **Only the `.exe` is uploaded:** the `.blockmap` file next to it is skipped.

**Left out, since not requested:**
- An action JSON so md2 can run the script.
- Building the installer inside the script.
- A CI workflow.

Say if you want any of these added.

**Note on `design/releases/0.8.0`:** it has no `release_notes.md`, so the script would refuse to publish 0.8.0.

author:

title: write release script

---
write a script that will:

* create a new tag on github with the current release number as can be read in [package.json](desktop/package.json)
* use that tag to create a new release on github. 
  * use the version as the release title
  * for the release notes, use the release\_notes.md files saved in the latest release folder, a sub folder of  `design\releases`. This folder will have as name, the current release number where the '.' are replaced with '\_'
  * upload the latest build found in `{{repository-folder}}/release`.  filename will be MD2-Setup-{{version}}-x64 where {{version}} is the release version.
* publish that release

## Current state

* Version source: `desktop/package.json` `version` (now `0.8.3`). `scripts/update_version.ps1` sets it in `app/` and `desktop/` `package.json`. `desktop/packaging/BUILDING_WINDOWS.md` names `desktop/package.json` authoritative.
* Build: `npm run build:windows` (`desktop/packaging/build_windows.js`) writes signed installer to `release/MD2-Setup-<version>-x64.exe` at repository root. Name comes from `artifactName` in `desktop/packaging/builder_config.js`. No electron-builder `publish` config exists.
* Release notes: complete-release flow (`app/src/services/release_operations.ts`) moves cards into `design/releases/<release name>`; folder name is release name typed by user. Latest folder `design/releases/0.8.3` uses dots, so script uses version unchanged as folder name (user decision; spec text about `_` is superseded). Older folders use `_` (`0_7_0`); `0.8.0` has no `release_notes.md`.
* `release_notes.md` starts with frontmatter (`---` block holding `internalId`), then `# MDÂ² <version>` and bullets. Frontmatter is md2 metadata, not release text.
* Existing git tags use `V_0_7_1` style. New script uses `v<version>` (user decision), e.g. `v0.8.3`. Old tags untouched.
* No GitHub release tooling in repository: no `.github/workflows`, no release script. `gh` (GitHub CLI) not installed on this machine. Remote `origin` \= [`https://github.com/jan-bogaerts/md2.git`.](https://github.com/jan-bogaerts/md2.git.)
* Script precedent: `scripts/update_version.ps1` (PowerShell 5.1, `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'`, `throw` on invalid input) with plain-PowerShell test `scripts/update_version.test.ps1`.

## Implementation details

New file `scripts/publish_release.ps1`. Runs from any working directory; resolves repository root via `Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot`. No parameters: version always read from `desktop/package.json`.

Prerequisite (document in script header comment): `gh` installed and authenticated (`gh auth login`) with push and release rights on `origin`.

Steps, in order. Every validation runs before first remote change, so failed validation changes nothing on GitHub:

1. Read `desktop/package.json` (UTF-8), parse with `ConvertFrom-Json`, take `version`. Missing or non-string: `throw`.
2. Derive values once: `$tag = "v$version"`, release title \= `$version`, notes path \= `design/releases/$version/release_notes.md`, installer path \= `release/MD2-Setup-$version-x64.exe`.
3. Validate:
   * `gh` available (`Get-Command gh`); else `throw` with install hint.
   * Notes file exists; else `throw` naming expected path.
   * Installer file exists; else `throw` naming expected path. Script never builds.
   * Tag absent locally (`git tag --list $tag`) and on `origin` (`git ls-remote --tags origin refs/tags/$tag`); else `throw` "Tag already exists". Prevents re-publishing same version.
4. Notes text: read notes file, strip leading frontmatter block (first line `---` up to next `---` line), trim. Empty result: `throw`. Write text to temporary file (`[System.IO.Path]::GetTempFileName()`, UTF-8 without BOM); delete it in `finally`.
5. Create annotated tag on current `HEAD`: `git tag -a $tag -m "MDÂ² $version"`. Push: `git push origin $tag`. HEAD means commit currently checked out; user is responsible for checking out release commit.
6. Create draft release with asset: `gh release create $tag $installerPath --title $version --notes-file $notesFile --verify-tag --draft`. `--verify-tag` makes `gh` fail instead of silently creating tag on GitHub. Draft keeps release hidden until upload finished.
7. Publish: `gh release edit $tag --draft=false`.
8. After each `git`/`gh` call check `$LASTEXITCODE`; non-zero: `throw` with command and step. Native commands do not trigger `$ErrorActionPreference`.
9. Output release URL (`gh release view $tag --json url --jq .url`).

Failure modes:

* Failure after tag push (step 6 or 7): tag and maybe draft stay on GitHub. Script does not roll back; error message lists cleanup: `gh release delete $tag --cleanup-tag` and `git tag -d $tag`. Rationale: rollback of remote state adds complexity for rare case.
* Only `.exe` uploaded; `.blockmap` excluded (spec names only installer; no auto-update consumes blockmap).

New test `scripts/publish_release.test.ps1`, same style as `scripts/update_version.test.ps1`. Fixture temp folder holds copied script, `desktop/package.json`, notes file, dummy installer. Test defines PowerShell functions `git` and `gh` before invoking script; functions take precedence over executables, so calls are recorded, nothing external runs. Stubs set `$global:LASTEXITCODE`.

Out of scope (not requested): action JSON in `design/actions` to run script from md2, building installer, CI workflow, renaming old tags or folders.

## Acceptance criteria

* Running `powershell -NoProfile -File scripts/publish_release.ps1` with version `0.8.3`, existing `design/releases/0.8.3/release_notes.md` and `release/MD2-Setup-0.8.3-x64.exe`:
  * creates and pushes annotated tag `v0.8.3` on `HEAD`;
  * creates published (non-draft) GitHub release for `v0.8.3` titled `0.8.3`;
  * release body equals `release_notes.md` content without frontmatter;
  * release has one asset `MD2-Setup-0.8.3-x64.exe`;
  * prints release URL.
* Missing notes file, missing installer, missing `gh`, or existing tag (local or `origin`): script exits non-zero with message naming cause; no tag created, nothing pushed, no `gh release` call.
* Failing `git`/`gh` call stops script with non-zero exit; message names failed step; after tag push, message includes cleanup commands.
* Temporary notes file removed on success and failure.
* `scripts/publish_release.test.ps1` covers: happy path (recorded `git`/`gh` arguments in order, notes without frontmatter), each validation failure (no remote-changing call recorded), non-zero exit from stubbed `gh release create`. Runs without network, git, or `gh`.

entries.content:
# Signed Windows package

Run from repository root:

```powershell
npm run build:windows
```

This command builds React first, then creates signed Windows x64 artifacts in `release/`:

- `MD2-Setup-<version>-x64.exe`
- `MD2-<version>-win-x64-unpacked/`

`desktop/package.json` is authoritative for product version. Packaging fails if React build, required packaged files, signing, timestamp, publisher verification, or artifact checks fail.

## Signing configuration

Always set `WIN_CSC_PUBLISHER_NAME` to text present in certificate subject. This value verifies both executable and installer after packaging.

For exportable PFX/P12 certificates, provide secrets through local or CI secret storage:

- `WIN_CSC_LINK`: secure file path, URL, or base64 certificate value supported by electron-builder.
- `WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD`: certificate password.
- `WIN_CSC_PUBLISHER_NAME`: expected certificate publisher.

For hardware-backed certificates or certificates installed in Windows certificate store, do not export key. Configure one or both selectors:

- `WIN_CSC_SUBJECT_NAME`: certificate subject name.
- `WIN_CSC_SHA1`: certificate thumbprint.
- `WIN_CSC_PUBLISHER_NAME`: expected certificate publisher.

Build uses SHA-256 signing, mandatory signing, and DigiCert RFC 3161 timestamp service. Never place certificate files, passwords, private keys, or encoded certificates in repository files, `.env` files, command arguments, logs, or package folders.

## Local and CI checks

Before release, run `npm run lint` and `npm run test` in both `app/` and `desktop/`. Build command also runs React typecheck/build and checks ASAR contents, production dependencies, renderer assets, forbidden certificate/source-map files, development-server URL, executable signature, installer signature, publisher, and timestamp.

Smoke-test unpacked application and installed NSIS build with Vite stopped and network disconnected. Open local Git project; read and edit file, commit, list branches, and invoke action. Install over prior version and confirm desktop settings remain present.
